metadata.summary: Thessalonica was a free city, provincial center, road junction, and harbor on the Thermaic Gulf in Roman Macedonia. Acts 17 narrates a mission involving Paul and Silas, synagogue hearers, Jason, political accusations, and politarchs; First Thessalonians directly addresses the resulting assembly, while the historical placement of Second Thessalonians depends partly on its disputed authorship and date.

relevance_metadata.parent_title: Thessalonica

evidence_items.claim: The city stood on the Via Egnatia at the head of the Thermaic Gulf and retained free-city institutions within Roman provincial rule. Pliny names its status; inscriptions attest politarchs; coins, sanctuaries, votives, associations, and later urban and funerary remains document a socially unequal and religiously plural city. These sources do not identify the assembly's building, full demographics, opponents, or every civic procedure narrated in Acts.

relevance_metadata.parent_title: Thessalonica

evidence_items.claim: Acts places the mission in a synagogue and names Jewish, God-fearing Greek, and prominent female hearers. First Thessalonians suggests substantial gentile participation, but neither source gives a demographic census or warrants collective Jewish blame for the assembly's affliction.
